text: This Motion seeks to release $7,500 of Section 37 funds to Heritage Toronto for a heritage plaque commemorating Greenwood Avenue's History of Brickmaking. Greenwood Avenue, south of Danforth Avenue, was Toronto's brickmaking capital in the 19th and 20th centuries. From the 1860's to the 1920's, there were at least 10 brickyards located along Greenwood Avenue that produced hundreds of thousands of bricks annually and employed hundreds of people. They included John Price Brick Maker, Morley and Ashbridge Brick Manufacturers, Taylor Brickyard, Logan Brickyards, John Price Brickyards, Wagstaff Brick Yards, the Isaac Price Brickyards, and more. The soil in the area was perfect for brickmaking and thousands of homes and buildings in Toronto were built from bricks made on Greenwood Avenue, Greenwood Park, the Greenwood subway yard, and many of the post-1940 housing developments on the east…

City Council on July 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 30, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council increase the 2018 Approved Operating Budget for Heritage Toronto by $7,500.00 gross, $0 net, (HG0001) fully funded by Section 37 community benefits obtained in the development 319 Carlaw Avenue (Source Account: XR3026-3700368), for the production and installation of a Heritage Plaque commemorating Greenwood Avenue's History of Brickmaking.
